title: Kernel-aware decode broker with hysteresis-based acceptance and graceful fallback
creator: Ava Chen
description: Proposal to implement a kernel-aware decode broker that coordinates prefill and decode stages across heterogeneous model variants and kernel implementations. The broker will use lightweight probe runs and a hysteresis-based acceptance mechanism to safely route requests to optimistic (fast) decode paths and fall back to conservative paths when acceptance confidence deteriorates. This aims to reduce end-to-end latency for common short-generation workloads while keeping rollout risk low through measurable acceptance metrics and automatic graceful fallback.
proposal: Design summary: (1) Kernel Advisor: at request start the broker profiles candidate kernels (CUDA/FP16 int8 kernels, Triton kernels, and CPU fallback) using a micro-probe that evaluates a 4-token prefill segment for latency and numeric stability characteristics (KV cache mismatch score, attention energy delta). Profiles are cached per model-version/sequence-length bucket. (2) Hysteresis Acceptance: acceptance is not a single boolean; it is a moving-state machine with three states: UNKNOWN -> PROBING -> STABLE_FAST. Transitions require statistical evidence over a sliding window: top-1 logit gap, softmax entropy delta, and top-k overlap with a conservative decode on probe runs. We require N_accept consecutive probes (default N=3) or a moving-average confidence above threshold to commit to STABLE_FAST. If acceptance dips below a lower hysteresis threshold for M tokens (default M=2), broker reverts to CONSERVATIVE path. (3) Fast-path behavior: once in STABLE_FAST, use optimized kernels and memory layouts (packed KV, grouped multihead attention optimization, fused rotary/ALiBi). Fast-path supports soft-commit: ephemeral tokens flagged as 'tentative' until sufficient acceptance window; these tentative outputs stream to the client with an 'optimistic' flag. (4) Fallback: on fallback, broker can either (A) soft-rollback: continue decode on conservative path and mark previously emitted tentative tokens as tentative/invalidated in stream metadata or (B) full-replay: replay decode from the last safe checkpoint using conservative kernels and re-emit canonical tokens. Choice is configurable by route/tenant. (5) Kernel mismatch heuristics: quantify kernel numeric divergence using per-layer L2 of attention weights and KL of logits for probe segments; those signals feed acceptance score. (6) Rollout controls: canary by user cohort, token-level telemetry, and automatic abort on sustained error rates.
acceptance_criteria: P50 latency improvement >= 18% on web-chat short-gen workload vs current conservative runtime when fast-path engaged
Acceptance false-commit rate <= 1% (fraction of requests where fast-path accepted but final conservative decode disagrees on first emitted token)
Rollback rate <= 0.5% in production canary (per 10k requests)
End-to-end cost reduction >= 10% for applicable workloads at 95% confidence in A/B test
No high-severity numeric regressions: per-layer attention L2 divergence under configured per-model threshold across probe suite
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge feature-flagged canary implementation behind runtime-2.3 flag; unit tests and CI pipeline
Week 1: Internal dogfood on staging with low-traffic tenant group; gather telemetry and tune thresholds
Week 2: Canary in prod for <1% traffic with soft-commit streaming enabled; collect acceptance and rollback metrics
Week 3: Evaluate metrics vs acceptance_criteria; if met, expand to 10% with automated abort thresholds; else iterate thresholds and kernel cache heuristics
Week 4-5: Gradual ramp to wider traffic and enable fast-path by default for non-sensitive tenants; monitor for regressions and disable automatically if rollback rate exceeds 0.5% over 1 hour
